links.targetTitle: Active Data Controllers may reference their own Active Data
Budget Controllers are the single sanctioned path from Atlas

title: Active Data is the one Supporting Document type modifiable outside the governance process
content:
A.1.2.2.1.3 establishes that most Supporting Document types "can be freely modified through the governance processes specified elsewhere in the Atlas," and then carves out one exception: "The Active Data Supporting Document type can be modified in real time by processes outside of said governance processes."

This solves a structural problem the Atlas creates for itself. A document tree whose categories encode mutability, and whose amendment runs through weekly and monthly governance cycles, cannot hold values that change daily — balances, lists, current parameters. Without an escape valve, either the tree goes stale or governance is flooded with bookkeeping.

A.1.1.3.1 shows the pattern in use: the list of Atlas Interpretations is Active Data, with an explicitly named Responsible Party (the Core Facilitator) and a named Update Process ('Direct Edit'). So the exception is not unbounded — real-time modification is traded for named accountability and a declared update protocol on each Active Data Controller.

The design principle generalizes: separate **state** from **rules**. Rules live in categories whose mutability is governed by position in the tree; state lives in a type that is explicitly allowed to move fast, on the condition that someone is on the record as responsible for it. The risk it accepts is that content which is really a rule gets classified as data to gain the fast path.
description: A.1.2.2.1.3 lets Active Data be updated in real time, creating a sanctioned channel for fast-moving state inside a slow-moving document tree — governed by a named Responsible Party instead of a vote.
